jobs.title: Implementation Specialist
jobs.description:
**About UKON**

UKON exists to help every business survive a cyberattack.  
Formerly known as FifthWall Solutions, we have grown from our foundation as a specialized cyber insurance wholesaler into a full-service cyber revenue partner for independent insurance agencies and managed service providers. We give our partners the technology, processes, carrier access, and expertise they need to deliver sophisticated cyber capabilities without the cost and complexity of building an internal cyber department.  
Today, our team works inside our partners’ books of business to identify uninsured companies, understand their risk, secure the right coverage, and help get more businesses protected. With access to more than 50 carriers and differentiated coverage options, including custom endorsements for emerging risks such as agentic AI, we help businesses understand what they are buying and how their coverage will respond when they need it most.  
We are building the AI-native operating system that will make this work scalable. Our platform brings together fragmented agency data, cybersecurity context, carrier appetite, quoting, communications, and workflows to shorten the distance between an uninsured business and a protected one.  
For us, AI-native does not mean adding a chatbot to an existing product. It means embedding intelligence throughout the platform so the system can understand the context of a user’s work, recommend the right next action, and help complete that action within the workflow. Because we operate in insurance, we care as much about accuracy, reliability, auditability, data privacy, and user control as we do about model capability.  
Our mission is ambitious but simple: close the estimated $10 trillion cyber protection gap and ensure every business can survive a cyberattack.

**The Role**

You will be UKON's first Implementation Specialist, reporting to our executive team and working closely with our product, sales, and Cyber Practice Leaders (CPLs), teams. This is a greenfield role. You are being hired to build it.

UKON partners with independent insurance agencies and managed service providers to deliver an outsourced cyber practice. Signing a partnership is only the beginning. Implementation turns a signed agreement into an active, growing agency relationship: getting the agency onboarded, trained, connected to their CPL, and producing. Today that process runs on effort and goodwill. Your job is to turn it into a repeatable system.

You will design the agency onboarding standard, the handoff from sales to CPLs, the training standards, and the implementation playbook, and then run them. You will decide what good looks like, measure it, and keep improving it. This starts as an individual contributor role, with the opportunity to own and grow the implementation function as UKON scales.

Experience implementing technology and managing projects matters more to us than experience in insurance. If you’ve helped customers get up and running on a SaaS or technology product, kept projects on track, and built or improved the process along the way, we want to talk to you.

**What You'll Do**

* Build UKON's agency onboarding standard from the ground up, from signed agreement to active, producing partner.
* Design and run the handoff process between sales and Cyber Practice Leaders so nothing is lost between signature and launch.
* Create training standards and materials that get agencies and their producers confident and active quickly.
* Write and maintain the implementation playbook, including operating procedures, checklists, timelines, and escalation paths.
* Own the implementation pipeline for new agency partners and keep every account moving forward.
* Define implementation metrics, track progress, and report on what is working and what is not.
* Identify where agencies stall after signing and fix the root cause, whether it sits in process, product, or people.
* Partner with sales, CPLs, marketing, and product to feed agency feedback back into how we sell, support, and build.
* Use project management and AI tools to run implementation efficiently and at scale.

**What You Bring**

* At least 5 years of onboarding, implementation, or customer success experience with SaaS or technology products.
* A track record of building operating procedures and processes from scratch, not just following existing ones.
* Project management experience, including running multiple concurrent implementations with tools like Asana, Monday, ClickUp, or similar.
* Exceptional attention to detail and a process-driven, high-ownership approach to your work.
* The relational skill to work across sales, CPLs, and agency partners and earn their trust.
* Comfort coordinating and directing the work of others, even without formal authority.
* Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to turn messy processes into simple, usable documentation.
* Comfort operating in ambiguity and creating structure where none exists.

**Bonus Points**

* Experience in insurance, insurtech, or another regulated industry.
* Familiarity with independent insurance agencies, agency management systems, or managed service providers.
* Exposure to product management or experience feeding customer input into a product roadmap.
* Experience as an early hire who built an implementation or onboarding function.
* A property and casualty insurance license, or interest in obtaining one.

**What Success Looks Like**

* Every new agency partner follows a clear, documented path from signed agreement to active production.
* Sales and CPLs trust the handoff process, and agencies feel supported from day one.
* More signed agencies become active, producing partners, and they get there faster.
* UKON has an implementation playbook that can scale as we add partners and team members.
* Leadership has clear visibility into implementation progress and where agencies need help.

**Travel**
----------

This role requires travel of approximately 10 to 20 percent, including visits to agency partners and industry events.

**Compensation and Benefits**
-----------------------------

**Pay range:** 100,000 - 120,000 USD per year base salary, plus a variable bonus of up to 20,000 USD per year.

**Benefits:** Medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401(k); paid time off and paid holidays; and stock options.

**Application deadline:** Applications will be accepted through November 15, 2026. This posting may close earlier if the position is filled.

As a temporary employee of GVSU, the Centralized Client Onboarding Specialist serves as the critical "front door" for the Michigan SBDC, welcoming and onboarding new clients into our organization. Specialists will use standardized scripts, triage logic, scheduling, CRM, and AI systems to ensure every client is efficiently assessed and matched with the right consultant based on region and expertise.

**1. Call Management & Client Triage**

* **Intake Execution:** Provide a professional, consistent, and welcoming first point of contact for all clients.
* **Welcome Meetings:** Prepare for and conduct scheduled phone calls with potential new clients. Introduce Michigan SBDC services, gather accurate information to confirm eligibility for no cost consulting, and route clients to the appropriate consultant.
* **Inbound Call Routing:** Manage and triage inbound calls to the primary client-facing phone number.
* **Complex Case Escalation:** Escalate complex client inquiries or system discrepancies to the Centralized Client Intake Manager for resolution.

* **Calendar Management:** Utilize Google Workspace and Calendly for all onboarding sessions to prevent double-bookings.

* **Protocol Adherence:** Strictly follow all standardized scripts, knowledge bases, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) developed by the Lead Center.
* **Session Tracking:** Accurately log data and information for each onboarding session for use in consulting and reporting.

jobs.description:
**Tallyforth Software**  
*From booked job to paid invoice.*

Tallyforth develops scheduling, dispatch, quoting, and invoicing software for commercial cleaning, landscaping, electrical, and property-maintenance companies. Customers use the platform to manage field employees, recurring work, customer records, and payments. The company is headquartered in Kansas City and employs a distributed team across the United States.

**Software Implementation Specialist**

**Location:** Remote within the United States  
**Work arrangement:** Fully remote, with optional access to the Kansas City office  
**Employment:** Full-time, salaried and exempt  
**Schedule:** Monday–Friday, with core availability from 10:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. Central Time  
**Hours:** Approximately 40 hours per week  
**Base salary:** $72,000–$88,000 per year, depending on relevant implementation experience and demonstrated technical skills  
**Annual bonus:** Target bonus of 8% based on individual objectives and company performance  
**Travel:** Up to 10% for selected customer launches and company meetings  
**Sales quota:** None  
**Reports to:** Implementation Team Lead  
**Direct reports:** None

The role

Tallyforth is hiring a Software Implementation Specialist to help new customers configure the platform, prepare their data, train employees, and complete a successful launch.

You will typically manage 8–10 active customer implementations with timelines of approximately 6–10 weeks. The position does not require software development, advanced programming, or responsibility for selling additional products.

What you will do

* Lead implementation kickoff meetings and confirm the customer’s goals, timeline, participants, and launch requirements.
* Learn how the customer currently schedules work, dispatches employees, prepares quotes, and issues invoices.
* Configure user permissions, service categories, workflows, forms, notifications, and account settings.
* Guide customers through standardized employee, customer, service, and pricing data imports.
* Review spreadsheet and CSV files for formatting issues before data is uploaded.
* Deliver remote administrator and end-user training sessions.
* Maintain an implementation plan with clear tasks, owners, deadlines, risks, and decisions.
* Test configured workflows and help customers complete launch-readiness checks.
* Escalate technical defects, unusual data requirements, and integration questions to the appropriate internal team.
* Document the final configuration and transfer the account to customer support and account management after launch.

What you need

* At least two years of experience in software implementation, customer onboarding, customer success, technical support, business systems, or another client-facing software role.
* Experience leading customer meetings and explaining software to users with different levels of technical experience.
* Strong spreadsheet skills, including sorting, filtering, basic formulas, data cleanup, and CSV formatting.
* Ability to manage several customer projects without losing track of decisions or deadlines.
* Clear written communication and organized documentation.
* Confidence learning configurable software and troubleshooting routine workflow problems.
* Availability during the stated Central Time core hours.

A bachelor’s degree is not required. Equivalent experience gained through customer operations, project work, software support, military service, or technical training may qualify.

Experience with CRM, scheduling, accounting, payroll, field-service, or workforce-management software is helpful. SQL, API development, and programming experience are not required.

Workload and customer schedule

Implementation specialists normally attend two to four customer meetings per day. The remaining time is reserved for configuration, data review, testing, documentation, and internal collaboration.

Customer meetings are scheduled during standard U.S. business hours. Occasional early or late meetings may be required for customers in different time zones, but employees may adjust their schedule on those days.

Weekend work is not normally required. A planned weekend launch may occur fewer than four times per year and requires the employee’s agreement and at least two weeks’ notice.

What success looks like

During the first 60 days, you will complete product training, observe implementations, practice configuration in a test environment, and begin supporting lower-complexity customers.

By six months, you should be able to independently manage a standard implementation from kickoff through launch and customer handoff.

Performance is evaluated through configuration accuracy, customer readiness, project documentation, appropriate escalation, customer feedback, and successful handoffs. Employees are not rewarded for launching an account before the customer is adequately prepared.

Compensation and benefits

Starting salary is determined by relevant SaaS experience, implementation ownership, customer-training ability, spreadsheet proficiency, software-configuration skills, and experience managing concurrent projects.

The annual target bonus is 8% of base salary. Actual payment may range from 0% to 12% based on company performance and documented individual objectives. The bonus is not tied to product sales or customer upselling.

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance with company premium contributions, an HSA option with an employer contribution, and access to virtual primary and mental-health care.
* 401(k) plan with a dollar-for-dollar company match on the first 5% of eligible compensation.
* 20 days of paid time off, 48 hours of paid sick leave, 11 company holidays, and two paid company-wide rest days.
* Twelve weeks of paid parental leave, company-paid life insurance, and short- and long-term disability coverage.
* Company-provided laptop, a one-time home-office allowance of $1,000, and a monthly internet and mobile-phone allowance of $100.
* Up to $2,000 annually for approved software, project-management, customer-training, or professional-development courses.
* Employee assistance and financial-guidance resources, plus company-paid travel for an annual team meeting.

How the team works

Implementation specialists own their customer projects but can request assistance from technical support, product, data operations, and account management. Complicated issues are assigned to the appropriate team instead of being left with one employee to solve alone.

The team documents configuration decisions and discusses risks early. Specialists are expected to be honest about timelines and product limitations, even when a customer is requesting a faster launch.

Hiring process

* A 30-minute introductory call with a Customer Operations Recruiter.
* A 45-minute interview with the Implementation Team Lead covering your customer-facing experience, software knowledge, and approach to managing multiple projects.
* A 60-minute live implementation scenario using a sample customer account and a small spreadsheet provided during the interview. You will explain how you would organize the launch, identify data issues, and prepare the customer for training. No advance preparation or take-home work is required.
* A 45-minute panel conversation with an Implementation Specialist and a Technical Support representative.
* Final reference and employment-verification checks, followed by a written offer.

Pay: $72,000.00 - $88,000.00 per year

Work Location: Remote
